title: Approval latency + sampling model for customer VPC changes (WIP)
content:
Status: WIP - sketching a measurable approval latency SLA and a low-cost sampling model for customer-managed VPC/network changes.

Context and why this matters
- Private deployments require customer-managed networking changes for things like peering, NAT gateways, customer SAN updates, firewall rules, and route-table edits. These changes often cross the boundary between Redwood operators and customer infra teams.
- We need two complementary systems: (1) a service-level expectation (SLA) for how long approval/attestation should take when customers request network changes, and (2) a telemetry + sampling model that provides forensic audit coverage without overwhelming storage/ingest or leaking PII.
- Current state: ad-hoc approvals, inconsistent logs across customer connectors, and overloaded oncall during churny periods. QA/Compliance asks for demonstrable median and p95 approval times and an evidence trail per approved change.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Define clear, measurable approval latency targets for each change class (minor config, standard change, network-impacting).
- Design a sampling/retention policy that guarantees 100% metadata capture for all approvals and selective full-packet/flow evidence for a smaller fraction (configurable per customer).
- Build operator UIs and runbooks to meet latency targets and telemetry SLIs.
- Ensure audit artifacts are linkable to attestation tokens and immutable logs for compliance review.

Change classes and target latency (proposed)
1) Minor config (e.g., tag changes, cosmetic route labels): target median approval <= 10 minutes, p95 <= 1 hour. Automated gating allowed; can be auto-approved if preconditions satisfied.
2) Standard change (e.g., change to customer-originated route prefixes, new peering): target median <= 30 minutes, p95 <= 4 hours. Requires operator attestation or delegated approver.
3) Network-impacting (e.g., modifying NAT firewall that can affect production traffic): target median <= 2 hours, p95 <= 8 hours. Requires multi-party approval and may trigger escalations.
4) Emergency rollback (customer-requested or operator-initiated): target median <= 15 minutes, p95 <= 1 hour. Separate fast-track SOP.

Rationale: buckets balance speed for low-risk ops with more rigorous checks for high-risk actions. Targets are intentionally conservative to allow human review but still predictable for customers.

Sampling & telemetry model
- Always-capture metadata: For every approval event, capture the following fields (100%): change_id, customer_id, actor (operator or customer principal), change_class, requested_at, approved_at, approvers (list), approval_policy_version, policy_trigger, precondition_checks (pass/fail list), attestation_token_id.
- Evidence tiering (sampled):
  * Tier A (full artifact): complete diffs, syslog snapshots, packet-capture snippet (if available), config blobs (sensitive fields redacted), pre/post state. Retain for 90 days by default.
  * Tier B (reduced artifact): config diffs + operator notes + summary traces, no raw packets. Retain for 365 days.
  * Tier C (metadata-only): only the 100% metadata (retain 5 years for compliance).
- Sampling rules: default sampling rate = 5% Tier A, 20% Tier B, remainder Tier C. Sampling is weighted by risk score computed from heuristics (customer segment, change_class, time-of-day, prior incidents). High-risk changes (network-impacting, customers with >1 incident in 90d) are automatically escalated to Tier A.
- Customer-configurable policy: customers on Dedicated/Private can opt into higher artifact retention or higher Tier A sampling (contracted). Defaults apply for hosted customers.

Telemetry schema (notes for infra/observability)
- Single event type: vpc_change_approval_event (JSON). All fields are flat primitives or arrays of strings; avoid nested objects in the audit stream to simplify queryability.
- Key fields (strings/dates/arrays): change_id, cust_org, environment, change_class, risk_score, preconds_summary, operator_ids, approver_ids, artifacts_tier, artifact_locations (URIs), attestor_signature, proof_hash, approval_latency_ms, change_duration_ms, linked_incident_id.
- Logs flow: event -> immutable ledger (append-only blob store with per-customer encryption) + index written to RediSearch for fast querying. Artifacts (Tier A/B) stored in blob store with ACL referencing the change_id and attestation_hash.

Approval flow + operator UX considerations
- Approval pages should surface: precondition checks (green/red), risk score, suggested approvers (based on policy), artifact policy (what will be retained), and estimated SLA deadline.
- Operators can mark an approval as "expedited" with justification; expedited approvals are rate-limited and must be reviewed in weekly postmortems.
- System automatically creates an immutable approval record once the first approver clicks "attest": includes a timestamp and an HMAC-signed token.

Sampling decision examples (heuristics)
- Rule A: if change_class == "network-impacting" or risk_score >= 70 -> Tier A.
- Rule B: if customer_tier == "enterprise" and contract.audit_addon == true -> promote to Tier A or longer retention.
- Rule C: changes between 02:00-04:00am local customer time get +10% sampling because off-hours changes correlate with incidents.

SLOs / SLIs to track
- SLI: approval_latency_ms (median and p95) per change_class per customer tier. Target: median and p95 as above.
- SLI: percent_of_changes_with_full_artifact (global and by customer). Target baseline 5% Tier A.
- SLI: artifact_ingest_success_rate (>= 99.9%).
- SLI: immutable_event_write_success_rate (>= 99.99%).

Privacy & data minimization
- Redact sensitive fields by default (API keys, customer private certs). Offer a managed-escape hatch for enterprise customers who contract for full artifacts and are responsible for secure storage.
- Provide a per-customer retention policy UI and an export path for regulatory requests.

Failover & graceful degradation
- If artifact ingestion fails, event metadata must still be written to the immutable ledger, and an incident must be created automatically.
- If the immutable ledger is unavailable, approvals can continue but the system attaches a temporary local attestation and queues the event for replay; this path is rate-limited and monitored.

Operational playbooks (short)
- On backlog/latency spike: escalate to oncall, enable delegated approvals for low-risk classes, temporarily increase sampling for Tier B to triage incidents.
- Post-incident: collect all Tier A artifacts for affected time window, freeze related approvals for audit, and run root-cause analysis.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How much of Tier A can we feasibly retain without ballooning storage costs? (finance/infra input required).
- Should we provide customer-visible audit queries (self-serve) or require a Redwood support flow for artifact exports?
- How to standardize redaction rules across connectors (AWS, GCP, on-prem)?

Next steps & owners
- PD: finalize change_class taxonomy and embed into policy engine (owner: Asha).
- Observability: implement vpc_change_approval_event schema + minimum 100% metadata pipeline (owner: Elena).
- Infra: costing model for Tier A retention + S3 lifecycle policies (owner: Samir).
- Legal/Compliance: sign-off on retention baselines and redaction defaults (owner: Grace).

Suggested milestones (quarterly)
- Q1: land 100% metadata pipeline + immutable ledger prototype; ship SLI dashboards.
- Q2: implement sampling engine + operator UX visibility; trials with 3 pilot customers.
- Q3: finalize retention contracts and admin UI for per-customer policy.

Notes / working threads
- See PD-4123 for the initial spec and customer asks.
- Slack thread: #private-deployments (thread G9X7Y2KQ) has customer feedback from pilot.
- Confluence draft linked above contains the onboarding checklist and existing runbook fragments.

- {\n  "change_id": "chg-20250319-7a2f",\n  "cust_org": "acme-corp",\n  "change_class": "standard",\n  "risk_score": "42",\n  "requested_at": "2025-03-19T15:12:00Z",\n  "approved_at": "2025-03-19T15:34:00Z",\n  "approval_latency_ms": "1320000",\n  "artifacts_tier": "B",\n  "artifact_locations": ["s3://redwood-audit/acme/chg-20250319-7a2f/tierB.json"],\n  "attestor_signature": "sig:abc123"\n}
